enrichment.summary: Sylvan Learning Center will provide its Sylvan Sync one-on-one program, which gives each participating special education student 30 hours of academic help in English language arts and/or math. The agreement runs February 18 to June 30, 2021 and is capped at $90,000. The Board is approving it after the work period began.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Sylvan Learning Center - Special Education Department

enrichment.headline: Approves up to $25,000 for Corrina Hui, LLC to design Castlemont High's Sustainable Urban Design Academy
enrichment.summary: Corrina Hui, LLC will provide services to design the Sustainable Urban Design Academy at Castlemont High School, so students and teachers learn and use the principles of Liberatory Design Thinking. The agreement runs January 18 to June 30, 2021 and is capped at $25,000. The Board is approving it after the work period began.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Corrina Hui, LLC - Sustainable Urban Design Academy - Castlemont High School

enrichment.headline: Approves up to $33,925 for Bay Area Community Resources to pay stipends to Fremont High career program students
enrichment.summary: Bay Area Community Resources will issue stipends, paid from the agreement amount, to Fremont High School students enrolled in a Spring and Summer Career Exploration and Preparation Program. The agreement runs February 1 to May 31, 2021 and is capped at $33,925.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Bay Area Community Resources - High School Network

enrichment.headline: Approves up to $8,140 for Studio Pathways to run three student workshops at Westlake Middle School
enrichment.summary: Studio Pathways will lead three 2-hour workshops at Westlake Middle School, covering breaking barriers, visual making and storytelling, and creative dialog, movement and character development, to create what the text calls emancipatory learning experiences for all students. The agreement runs March 15 to May 27, 2021 and is capped at $8,140. The Board is approving it after the work period began.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Studio Pathways - Westlake Middle School

enrichment.headline: Approves up to $9,450 for racial equity coaching sessions for the Oakland Tech principal
enrichment.summary: An outside consultant based in Vallejo will provide racial equity executive coaching sessions for the principal of Oakland Technical High School. The agreement runs January 4 to June 30, 2021 and is capped at $9,450. The Board is approving it after the work period began.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Dante King - High School Network

enrichment.headline: Accepts $207,030 through Oakland Public Education Fund to expand tech support for students' devices
enrichment.summary: The district accepts a $207,030 regrant from the Oakland Public Education Fund, funded by the Charles and Lynn Schusterman Family Foundation. The money enhances and expands tech support for students and families using #Oakland Undivided devices. The grant period is October 28, 2020 to June 30, 2021.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Grant Agreement - Oakland Public Education Fund - Charles and Lynn Schusterman Family Foundation - Chief Academic Officer

enrichment.headline: Approves up to $8,740 for Destiny Arts Center's Zoom dance and self-defense classes at United for Success
enrichment.summary: Destiny Arts Center will lead daily Zoom activities and classes at United for Success Academy, including dance and self-defense and possibly Capoeira, Hip Hop or Percussion. The agreement runs August 24, 2020 to May 26, 2021 and is capped at $8,740. The Board is approving it after the work period began.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Professional Services Agreement 2020-2021 - Destiny Arts Center - United for Success Academy

enrichment.headline: Approves a standard agreement with outside groups that place students in workplace internships
enrichment.summary: This standard memorandum of understanding (MOU) clarifies the relationship between the district and third-party "intermediaries" that place students in workplace internships. Its terms cover sharing data on enrollment, academic performance and COVID exposures. The text lists no dollar amount.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Standard Memorandum of Understanding - Third Party Intermediaries - Workplace Student Internships - High School Linked Learning Office

enrichment.headline: Approves up to $25,000 for Cypress Mandela's five-week paid construction pre-apprenticeship for 30 students
enrichment.summary: Cypress Mandela Training Center will run a five-week paid pre-apprenticeship program in the construction trades for up to 30 high school students. Topics include project estimating, construction elements, project management, tools, resume writing, nutrition and interview skills. It runs June 16 to July 23, 2021 and is capped at $25,000.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Memorandum of Agreement - Cypress Mandela Training Center - Summer Program - High School Linked Learning Office

enrichment.headline: Approves a no-cost three-year agreement with Kaiser Oakland for teachers to instruct hospitalized children
enrichment.summary: This memorandum of understanding (MOU) and Business Associate Agreement with Kaiser Foundation Hospital Oakland/Richmond lets district teachers provide instruction for school-age children who are hospitalized at Kaiser Oakland. The text lists no dollar amount. The period is July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2023, and it began before the Board's approval.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Memorandum of Understanding and Business Associate Agreement - Kaiser Foundation Hospital Oakland/Richmond - High School Linked Learning Office

enrichment.headline: Accepts $50,000 from Kids In Need of Defense to build advocacy resources for unaccompanied immigrant youth
enrichment.summary: Kids In Need of Defense (KIND), based in Washington, D.C., is giving the district $50,000 to develop resources and trainings on effective advocacy for unaccompanied immigrant youth. The work will be run by the English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement Department from March 15, 2021 through January 31, 2023.

enrichment.headline: Applies for $105,000 from the Emerging Bilingual Collaborative for English language development materials
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving a grant application to the Emerging Bilingual Collaborative, a New Venture Fund project in Washington, DC, asking for $105,000. The money would go toward developing and putting in place high-quality English language development materials aligned to English language arts for grades K-8, from March 15 to June 30, 2021. This approves the application only; the funding is not yet awarded.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Grant Application - Emerging Bilingual Collaborative - Language Equity Through High Quality English Language Development (ELD) Instruction - English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement Department

enrichment.headline: Amends the Board's Parent Involvement policy (Board Policy 6020) for Title I
enrichment.summary: The Board is approving changes to Board Policy 6020, Parent Involvement, which covers Title I, the federal funding for schools serving many low-income students. The changes were proposed by the Office of Equity. The text of the changes is in the attached policy, not in this summary.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment, Board Policy - Instruction - BP 6020 - Parent Involvement

enrichment.headline: Asks the state for permission to monitor nonpublic schools virtually instead of on site
enrichment.summary: The Board is adopting a resolution that lets staff ask the California Department of Education for a waiver from the Education Code rule requiring on-site monitoring of nonpublic schools, which serve students with disabilities placed there by the district. If approved, monitoring could be done virtually. The item lists no fiscal impact.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Waiver Request - California Department of Education - To Permit Virtual Non-Public School Monitoring - Special Education Department

enrichment.headline: Adds $3,375 for ten more coaching hours for administrators at Rudsdale Continuation High School
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying (formally approving) a change to the district's agreement with Mills College for ten more hours of coaching for site administrator training at Rudsdale Continuation High School. The change adds $3,375 and raises the agreement's not-to-exceed amount from $2,700 to $6,075. All other terms stay the same.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 1, Professional Services Agreement - Mills College - Rudsdale Continuation High School

enrichment.headline: Approves up to $30,000 for Weinstein and Numbers LLP legal help on insurance and joint powers matters
enrichment.summary: The Board is ratifying (approving) an agreement with Weinstein and Numbers LLP, a law firm with Bay Area offices, to give the district legal services as needed on insurance and Joint Powers Agreement (JPA) matters. Payments cannot exceed $30,000 from February 16, 2021 through June 30, 2022. A Joint Powers Agreement lets public agencies share services such as insurance.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Memorandum of Understanding and Engagement Policy - Weinstein and Numbers LLP - General Counsel

enrichment.headline: Adds $184,000 to Lozano Smith's legal contract for property, construction and other district matters
enrichment.summary: The Board is increasing the cap on the district's agreement with the law firm Lozano Smith by $184,000, from $300,000 to $484,000, for the 2020-21 fiscal year. The added legal work covers facilities and construction, real estate, litigation and other topics, including a parcel swap with the City of Oakland at 1700 Market Street, long-term ground leases at Tilden and Shands, and a joint occupancy agreement for the new Piedmont library.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 2, Memorandum of Understanding and Engagement Policy - Lozano Smith, Attorneys at Law - General Counsel

enrichment.summary: The Board is adopting a resolution acknowledging that it received a letter from Roses in Concrete Community School promising to fund positions at Howard Elementary School. The resolution text does not state a dollar amount or time period.

outcome.action: Adopted

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

Reynolds for planning and facilitation at three more orientation meetings for the Board members serving as of January 4, 2021. The added $4,500 comes at no cost to the district and raises the not-to-exceed amount from $9,000 to $13,500. The funding source is listed as donations.
